name: Zendesk
subcategory: help desks, live chat and support knowledge
tagline: Operate a small email and web support inbox with tickets and an audit trail

pricing.notes: Official Suite Team monthly agent price.

tiers.name: Suite Team
tiers.limits: 5 automated resolutions/agent/month; 40,000 action credits/account/month; ticketing, messaging and help center

tiers.name: Suite Growth
tiers.limits: 10 automated resolutions/agent/month; 40,000 action credits/account/month; multiple help centers and SLAs

tiers.name: Suite Professional
tiers.limits: 10 automated resolutions/agent/month; 100,000 action credits/account/month; skills routing and advanced analytics

tiers.name: Suite Enterprise
tiers.limits: 15 automated resolutions/agent/month; 225,000 action credits/account/month; sandbox and advanced governance
tiers.notes: The current top-level page emphasizes a sales-assisted Enterprise + Copilot package; list prices remain documented by Zendesk Support.

tiers.name: Suite Enterprise Plus
tiers.limits: 15 automated resolutions/agent/month; 400,000 action credits/account/month; enhanced sandbox and disaster recovery
tiers.notes: Annual list price; no monthly list price is published.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; Enterprise Plus annual only at published list price
pricing.hiddenCosts: Automated-resolution allowances do not roll over; additional resolutions or overage are extra and current tiered pricing is sales/account-specific. Extra action credits cost $200 per 100,000. Copilot is $50/agent/month billed annually, Quality Assurance $35, and Advanced Data Privacy and Protection $50. Talk phone numbers, minutes and texts are usage-priced separately.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Zendesk, operate a small email and web support inbox with tickets and an audit trail. The hard boundary is omnichannel routing, marketplace, workforce tools, reporting, compliance, and support, plus channel integrations and support operations.
coreLoopDIY: Receive customer email and web messages, route them into a shared ticket inbox, reply from one place, and retain a searchable conversation history with an audit trail.
whatYouLose: omnichannel routing, marketplace, workforce tools, reporting, compliance, and support
ongoingBurden: message delivery, webhooks, threading, identity, permissions, attachments, notifications, spam, search, uptime, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Zendesk because support software survives because missing or misrouting one customer message is expensive and every channel behaves differently. The recurring cost buys message delivery, webhooks, threading, identity, permissions, attachments, notifications, spam, search, uptime, and retention, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Chatwoot
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source customer engagement and shared-inbox platform.

alternatives.name: Chatwoot
alternatives.desc: A proper support inbox with chat, email and a help center; free software, billable server chores.

facts.dataFormat: Conversations, contacts and configuration in PostgreSQL; Redis handles jobs and cache; attachments use local disk or configured object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It has less mature enterprise reporting, administration, marketplace integration and support operations than Zendesk, while self-hosting adds upkeep.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires a VM or Docker, PostgreSQL, Redis, SMTP, persistent or object storage, HTTPS, backups and upgrades

alternatives.name: Frappe Helpdesk
alternatives.desc: Tickets, SLAs and a knowledge base in a clean Frappe shell; the five-minute installer still leaves you the pager.

facts.install: Frappe Cloud signup or easy-install script, Bench or Docker
facts.dataFormat: Tickets and knowledge-base data in the Frappe site database; attachments in site file storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It is younger and narrower in channels, reporting, marketplace integrations and enterprise administration than Zendesk.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires Frappe Bench or Docker, MariaDB and Redis services, mail, a domain, backups and upgrades

alternatives.name: FreeScout
alternatives.desc: Email becomes an assigned team inbox with notes and collision warnings; the nicer modules open a wallet.

facts.install: Upload the PHP application and run its Laravel web installer
facts.dataFormat: Mailbox, ticket and contact data in MySQL or MariaDB; attachments in application storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It is primarily an email help desk, with fewer channels, weaker reporting and automation, and paid add-on modules where Zendesk is more integrated.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP and a web server, MySQL or MariaDB, cron, IMAP or SMTP or OAuth, backups and separately paid modules for several extras

alternatives.name: osTicket
alternatives.desc: Email and web forms become assigned tickets; dated, dependable and very much your PHP server.

facts.install: Upload the release archive to a PHP and MySQL web server and run the installer
facts.dataFormat: Tickets, users and messages in MySQL; attachments can be kept in the database or configured filesystem storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its interface and workflows are dated and its automation, reporting, channel coverage and integration ecosystem trail Zendesk substantially.
facts.setupBlocker: PHP, MySQL, web-server permissions, inbound and outbound mail, cron and backups

alternatives.name: Zammad
alternatives.desc: A serious ticket desk with email, chat, SLAs and a knowledge base; setup is the first ticket.

facts.install: Hosted signup or Docker Compose, Portainer or OS package
facts.dataFormat: Tickets and users in PostgreSQL, queue and cache in Redis, search in Elasticsearch or OpenSearch, and attachments in filesystem or object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a serious desk but has a smaller marketplace and reporting ecosystem than Zendesk and a heavier self-hosted stack to operate.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting normally means Docker plus PostgreSQL, Redis, Elasticsearch or OpenSearch, mail channels, a domain and backups

alternatives.name: Odoo Helpdesk One App Free
alternatives.desc: A real hosted ticket desk for unlimited users, as long as Helpdesk is your one free Odoo app.

facts.dataFormat: Tickets, messages and attachments live in Odoo Online's managed database and filestore
facts.gapVsPaid: It has less mature omnichannel support, reporting, marketplace integration and enterprise administration than Zendesk.
facts.setupBlocker: None for Helpdesk alone; installing another Odoo app ends the one-app-free arrangement

alternatives.name: tawk.to
alternatives.desc: Live chat, tickets, email, and a help centre for zero dollars; the tiny tawk.to badge pays the rent.

facts.install: Hosted signup plus a JavaScript snippet or CMS plugin
facts.engines: tawk.to AI Assist; underlying models are not disclosed
facts.dataFormat: Chats, tickets and contacts live in tawk.to's cloud database until deleted; chat and ticket data can be exported
facts.gapVsPaid: Its ticketing, SLA, reporting, workflow and integration depth are much lighter than Zendesk's.
facts.setupBlocker: The website widget or plugin must be installed; removing tawk.to branding is paid

alternatives.name: LibreDesk
alternatives.desc: A modern email-and-live-chat desk in one compact stack, because apparently that was allowed.

facts.install: Docker or prebuilt binary with PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: Conversations, contacts, rules and settings in PostgreSQL; attachments live on the self-hosted instance or configured storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It is young and compact, with much less channel depth, reporting, marketplace integration and enterprise administration than Zendesk.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker or a binary plus PostgreSQL, mail channels, a domain, HTTPS, persistent storage and backups

rejectedAlternatives.name: FreeScout
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Email tickets are free; the customer portal and web form are a paid module.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Freshdesk Free Program
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free program expires after six months, so it cannot replace an ongoing desk.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Suite Team plan and a small-team shared inbox DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Zendesk in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, WebSockets, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: receive customer email and web messages, route them into a shared ticket inbox, reply from one place, and retain a searchable conversation history with an audit trail.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement one workspace, agents, contacts, inboxes, conversations, messages, labels, and assignment.
Provide a website chat widget with reconnect, unread counts, file limits, and clear availability state.
Create a shared inbox with filters, collision warnings, notes, canned replies, and searchable history.
Add email notifications, browser notifications, and an immutable assignment and status log.
Implement spam controls, attachment scanning hooks, retention settings, export, and contact deletion.
Ship Docker Compose, backups, health checks, migrations, and a documented admin recovery flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out many social and messaging channels.
Deliberately leave out AI agents trained on proprietary support data.
Deliberately leave out enterprise workforce management, SSO, and compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
